label: Game A
nuance_found: Kills build a score multiplier (x2 up to x5 seen), and BLOOM is a charge you pop for a BLOOMSTORM that floods a patch with colour and jumps the score (61,410 to 65,010 at x3 in one burst). The choice is when to spend BLOOM, but fire-at-the-nearest-blob is the obvious line and I never saw a reason to do anything else.
audio: A looping music bed under everything, procedural noise bursts for shots and hits, a falling saw tone when I took damage, and a chime on kills. Punchy, but little variety.
furthest_progress: Olive Terraces, still on the first objective 'Break the inkwell'. Never broke the inkwell. Score 88,940, x5 multiplier peak, 1.8% restored. Saw NODES OPEN once and 'THE INK TOOK YOU' once (one death seen clearly).
control_trouble: Aiming with the right-thumb drag was touchy, my turns often overshot, and I walked away from the gold marker many times, which cost a lot of the walking time. Some of that is the harness. The marker pinning to the screen edge also misled me.
best_moment: BLOOMSTORM at x3: the whole hillside burst into colour and the score jumped by about 3.6k.
worst_moment: Dying at the inkwell to tall ink figures I could not target, then a long slow walk back across a big grey map with nothing happening.
verdict: The score loop is the good part. Multiplier chains, bloomstorm bursts, colour flooding back and numbers flying. I understood it in about 25 s and wanted to chain it. But most of my time was a long slow walk across a big grey map, and the inkwell fight killed me with things I could not target, with nothing telling me what was hurting me. When I was in a pack of blobs with BLOOM ready it was a 7. The rest was a 4. I would try it once more, but I would not tell friends.
